spec_match.rationale: Buttons invoke the exact Working Draft surface — await window.maximize()/minimize()/restore() — and the readout uses the non-permission-gated (display-state: …) media feature, matching the chromestatus summary and the Window Management draft.

interactive.rationale: A per-method typeof probe grid, three real invocation buttons with a resolve/reject log, a live display-state readout with change listeners, and a clear-log control — no static code card.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The index blurb promises buttons that call the Promise-returning methods and report resolution vs unavailability; the page delivers exactly that with distinct resolved/rejected/not-exposed outcomes.

edge_cases.rationale: Handles method-absent (honest fallback log line, no fake result), rejection with error name/message, the installed-PWA + transient-activation + permission invocation conditions in the banner, and the no-value-matches media-state ambiguity.

references.rationale: See-also links https://chromestatus.com/feature/5201832664629248 plus the three sibling concepts.

conformance.rationale: The feature suite asserts each method's typeof against the draft, display-state/resizable active-value scripts, and three honestly-blocked manual assertions for installed-window transitions; in this Chromium 141 session it reports 0 pass / 6 fail / 3 blocked, all failures being the expected absent experimental surface, not demo defects.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Verified via headless Chromium 141 CLI/CDP (no chrome-devtools-mcp in this cloud session): desktop 1280×800 screenshot shows probe grid all undefined with the honest fallback log line, zero console errors, no failed same-origin requests; buttons could not be clicked in this non-interactive harness so resolve/reject paths were not driven.

telemetry_health.rationale: showcaseTelemetry.assert records the probe result and per-method resolved/rejected/unavailable outcomes with error names.

design_system.rationale: All colours are CSS variables, the secondary button overrides background and color together, and focus-visible outlines are defined.

accessibility.rationale: Native buttons with visible focus-visible outlines, the result log is role=log aria-live=polite with an aria-label, and state changes are surfaced as text.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: CDP-emulated mobile 360×740 DPR3 shows scrollWidth == innerWidth (0px overflow), wrapped flag-banner text, stacked probe cells and full-width tappable buttons; desktop 1280×800 clean; only the environmental fonts.googleapis.com stylesheet fails.

openQuestions.title: Capture installed-app success-path evidence once an implementing channel is available
openQuestions.detail: Every method resolves only in an installed desktop PWA with the enable-desktop-pwas-additional-windowing-controls flag, transient activation, and the window-management permission — none of which a headless browser-tab session can provide, so the resolved branch and the post-resolution display-state flip remain unverified. When a Chrome/Canary build with the flag and an installable window is available to the validation environment, drive maximize/minimize/restore end-to-end and record the resolved log lines plus the media-state transition, then update the three blocked manual conformance assertions' evidence.

summary: Honest, spec-exact probe-and-invoke page for the proposed window.maximize/minimize/restore surface with a live display-state readout and truthful unavailable/rejected handling. Verified with headless Chromium 141 via CLI/CDP (no chrome-devtools-mcp in this environment): clean console, no unintended failed requests, no mobile or desktop overflow, honest fallback shown since the experimental API is absent in this build; interactive success paths need an installed flagged window that this session cannot provide. Feature conformance route reports the expected unsupported-surface failures plus three honestly-blocked manual assertions.
